findings.description: The customer-managed KMS key used for the audit bucket does not enable automatic key rotation (enable_key_rotation defaults to false and no aws_kms_key_rotation resource is present), so the same key material is used indefinitely and a leaked or compromised key cannot be retired through routine rotation.

No key policy is specified for this customer-managed KMS key, so it falls back to the default policy granting the account root full control, including the ability to modify the key policy, disable the key, or schedule its deletion. Without an explicit least-privilege policy restricting which principals may administer and use the audit key, any account-level principal with key-management permissions can undermine the encryption of audit logs.
